messages:
Anya: Quick mock — can we tuck the token breakdown into an expandable row on invoices? Screenshots: https://img.redwood/mock/invoice-row.png Sam: I like the density win, especially for org-level invoices where rows get huge. Accordion seems fine. :+1: Maria: Heads-up: our analytics page expects a flat mapping per invoice for token counts. If we collapse into accordion, need to ensure indices still export cleanly. Taylor: Discoverability worry — users might miss the breakdown. Can we surface a short summary (e.g., "2.3k tokens — click to expand") inline? Also keyboard focus needs to land on the toggle. Anya: Great call. Proposed: show summary + chevron to expand. Default collapsed for org view, auto-expand for single-project invoice. Sam: Implementation note: we can reuse existing accordion component. Just add `data-invoice-row-id` so export job can still map. Maria: If you add `data-invoice-row-id` make sure the export lambda picks up nested rows — right now it only queries `.invoice-row` selectors. Might need to emit an explicit CSV row per expanded block. Taylor: Accessibility nit: toggle should be a `
...breakdown table...
``` Sam: One more perf thing: if many invoices on a page, expanding lots could blow up DOM and KV cache. Suggest we lazy-render breakdowns on first expand. Maria: +1 to lazy-render. Also for CSV/JSON export, we should allow a query param `expand=true` to include breakdown rows server-side so exports don't rely on client DOM. Taylor: Copy tweak: instead of "tokens" in the summary maybe use "compute units" in org-level view? Some finance folks prefer that language. But keep tokens on project-level invoices. Thoughts? Anya: Hmm. Risk of inconsistency. Maybe show both: "2,345 tokens (compute units: 2.3k)" — but that's noisy. Alternative: show a tooltip explaining equivalence when hovering the term. Sam: I'd avoid dual primary labels. Tooltip feels safest. design-bot: Accessibility checklist reminder: ensure contrast for chevron >= 4.5:1, focus ring visible, no reliance on color alone, state changes announced by screenreaders (e.g., aria-live for count updates). Anya: Thanks — I'll add aria-live to the count so when breakdown loads we `aria-live="polite"` update the summary. Maria: Timeline: can we get a dev estimate? Frontend + export changes + UX review. Sam: Ballpark: frontend 3-4 dev days (accordion + aria + lazy render), export endpoint 1-2 days, QA + accessibility review 1 day. Taylor: I'll do a quick keyboard walkthrough after the first PR. Anya: Cool — I'll push updated mock and a PR description with acceptance criteria: collapsed by default (org), summary visible, lazy render, server-side export toggle, aria attributes, tooltip copy. Sam: Sounds good. Assign to @sam for export work, @anya for frontend, @taylor for A11y review. :calendar: Maria: Thanks — let's aim to ship as a post-release patch so it doesn't block the billing dashboard rollout. Anya: Perfect. I'll post updated screenshots here when ready. :sparkles:
